title: Make the Intent sidebar easier to scan and hide

intentCoverage.report:
## Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-271#compact-intent-sidebar **Outcome: Caught.** - Story and revision: section `compact-intent-sidebar` in `.planning/seeds/SEED-271-compact-intent-sidebar.md`, key example 3. Revision 1609b010d377eb7fda82067149aa5eef470f3b3d (terryyin/open-dough). - Promise: with a story selected, Selected story only checked, the summary expanded, a file's Purpose open and the tree scrolled, Hide files and then Show files bring back the summary, the open folders, the selected file row and the tree's scroll. The reading pane still shows that file's Purpose. - Fault (location and change): `dashboard/src/IntentBrowser.tsx`, the `.intent-locations` column (about line 181). Instead of `
…
`, it rendered `files.shown ?
…
:
`. The column element is now unmounted on hide and recreated on show, instead of being hidden. A hidden placeholder keeps the toggle's `aria-controls` target, so the hide step still behaves correctly and the run reaches the restoration assertions. - Why not the exact suggested fault: rendering `{files.shown &&
…}` would fail early at the hide step, where `expectFilesShown` in `dashboard/tests/intentModePage.ts:67` reads the column's `id`. It would never reach the restoration path. - Fixture: the test's own setup through `selectTakenStoryInIntent(page, origin, changeWithDeepSpec)` at viewport 1280x560. It checks Selected story only, expands the summary, selects `deepSpec`, scrolls the tree halfway (offset > 20), then Hide files and Show files. - Maintained assertion: `dashboard/tests/intent/intent-sidebar-toggle.spec.ts`, test "Hide files gives the reading pane the width and the strip shows nothing of the summary; Show files returns the column as it was" (line 88). Its tree-scroll restoration check (lines 132-134) is `expect.poll(() => column(intent).evaluate(e => e.scrollTop)).toBe(offset)`. ### Run observations - Scratch checkout: a detached worktree at 1609b010d3, clean before the probe (empty `git status --porcelain`). Native npm and browser setup completed. - Command: `env -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR npm run test:dashboard -- tests/intent/intent-sidebar-toggle.spec.ts --reporter=list`. Global setup rebuilds the dashboard app on every run, so each run served the edited source. - Baseline: 4 passed, including the selected test at :88 (10.1s), in 16.3s. - Discarded first probe: I kept the column element and unmounted only its contents while hidden. The run passed (4 passed, 10.1s), but this fault produced no wrong behavior to detect: - Open folders, Selected story only, the expanded location and the reveal are kept in `useKeptArrangement` state (`pageIntentReading.tsx`, `useLocationOpenFolders.ts`, `useIntentStoryTree.ts`), so they come back after a remount. - The scroll container itself stayed mounted, so its scroll offset survived. - It is not counted as an assertion gap and not used as the outcome. - Faulted run (the fault above): exit 1. Only the selected test failed; the other 3 passed (13.0s). - Failure: `Expected: 110, Received: 0` at `intent-sidebar-toggle.spec.ts:134`, after the 5000ms poll timed out. - **Reach:** every earlier assertion in the test passed under the fault. That covers the hide-step layout and strip checks, `expectFilesShown(true)`, summary `aria-expanded="true"`, Selected story only checked, the selected file `aria-pressed="true"`, and the `boundary`/`deep` folders open. So the run reached the intended scroll-restoration assertion, and that assertion failed on the changed behavior: the recreated column started at scrollTop 0 instead of the 110 the developer had scrolled to. - The fault ran on the intended path, the column's hide/show rendering, and changed only that. - Restoration: I copied back the pre-probe file from a saved copy. `git status --porcelain` was empty, `git diff --quiet` was clean, and HEAD was still 1609b010d377eb7fda82067149aa5eef470f3b3d. The rerun with the same command passed 4 of 4 (the selected test 7.5s, total 10.3s). - Cleanup: the scratch worktree was removed with `git worktree remove --force`. The execution checkout was not edited. Its current staged deletions of the SEED-271 seed and the 525 plan files come from the concurrent wrap-up, not this check. - Side finding: the summary disclosure and the folder/selection state come back because they are kept application state, not because the column stays mounted. The maintained test's scroll assertion is the one that specifically guards "hidden, not unmounted." ### Cost - **Test runtime (measured, Playwright-reported wall time per run):** baseline 16.3s, discarded probe 10.1s, faulted run 13.0s, restored run 10.3s. Total 49.7s across 4 runs. This excludes npm, browser and dashboard build setup outside Playwright's reported time. - **Human effort:** unavailable. No human took part in this agent run, and there is no separate measure of human time. - **Agent effort:** unavailable. This agent cannot see a supported token or compute measure. Tool-call count (about 16 calls) is given only as an estimated proxy, not a measure of effort. - **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 155092 ms (measured), from 1794132409732 to 1794132564824 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.
